summary: The neutral stance held up on 11-03. The Portfolio Manager's decision reasoning records agreeing with the Market Analyst's neutral call. SPY's tracked value rose from 588.74 to 590.5 (cumulative return from -1.88% to -1.58%, about +0.3% on the day) and stayed 3.55% above its 200-day average (752.1 vs 726.3 at the 11-02 packet), so the regime filter stayed on and a neutral call neither missed a break nor a breakout. The tech and communication weakness in the packet (XLK 21d -12.81%, XLC 21d -9.12%, QQQ 21d -9.14% and only 0.35% above its 200-day) and the staples and health care leadership (XLP 21d +12.79%, XLV 21d +11.08%) were consistent with the PM's decision to add nothing in Technology. The account lost $0.72 on the day (equity $617.08, drawdown 0.1%), so no stance-driven damage. I did not re-read my own 11-03 output in this review because the role file does not list it as an input, so the sector and asset-class details below rest on the packet and the PM's quoted use of them.

(1) One day of SPY drift is thin evidence; my graded record is 6 right, 0 wrong, 5 pending (hit rate 1.0, enough_data false), and all graded calls are neutral on a flat-to-down SPY, so the record does not yet show that I can call risk-on or risk-off. Treat the 100% hit rate as unproven. (2) Defensive rotation is the main tape signal: staples and health care lead on 21 days while XLK is -12.81% over 21 days and -6.49% over 5 days, and gold (GLD 21d -4.86%, 12.35% under its 200-day) has not worked as a haven, while bonds have (TLT 21d +5.92%, IEF +3.10%, BND +2.35%). If QQQ closes below its 200-day (now only 0.35% above) the neutral stance should move toward risk-off for sizing. (3) Breadth is better than the index: RSP 21d +4.89% vs SPY -2.28%. The PM's VOO thesis invalidates on RSP turning negative over 21 days, so I should flag RSP direction in the next packet.
